deals.evidence: C'était la condition pour que l'homme d'affaire américain investisse ses 10 millions d'€ dans le club
deals.headline: US businessman Vincent Volpe takes over HAC with a €10m investment
deals.summary: Volpe made his €10m investment and takeover of the club conditional on a €4m arrangement with the Le Havre urban community (CODAH): three years without stadium rent in Ligue 2, and CODAH taking over equipment the club had installed at Stade Océane. He succeeded Jean-Pierre Louvel and owned the club until July 2025.

deals.date_text: Signed late June 2025; Blue Crow majority shareholder from July 2025
deals.evidence: sans préciser le montant du rachat des 96,21% que détenait Vincent Volpe
deals.headline: Blue Crow Sports Group buys Vincent Volpe's 96.21% of Le Havre AC
deals.summary: Blue Crow Sports Group, a US multi-club group that also owned Cancún FC and CD Leganés, bought the 96.21% stake held by Vincent Volpe. The price was not disclosed. Blue Crow presented its project on 2 July 2025, and the club dates Blue Crow's majority ownership from July 2025. Law firm Ebadat announced on 23 July 2025 that it had advised on the completed acquisition. 76actu reported that the deal cleared debt estimated at at least €5m. Press headlines in July 2026 reported dueling lawsuits in Texas over the purchase.

deals.evidence: The Dubai-based investment firm 885 Capital bought a significant share in Blue Crow this year
deals.headline: UAE-based 885 Capital buys a significant share of Blue Crow Sports Group, HAC's owner (parent-level)
deals.summary: The Guardian reported that Dubai-based investment firm 885 Capital bought a significant share in Blue Crow in 2025. Sportico (July 2025) described 885 as a co-owner of Blue Crow, but not the only one. This is an indirect, parent-level stake; no percentage is published. In June 2026 Blue Crow sold its 84.21% of CD Leganés to 885 Capital, so 885's current position in Blue Crow is not confirmed.

deals.date_text: May 2026 (extraordinary general meeting; subscriptions open to 8 June 2026)
deals.evidence: ce que l'on sait déjà, c'est que Blue Crow y contribuera à hauteur de 18 M€
deals.headline: Blue Crow commits €18m to a HAC capital increase
deals.summary: An extraordinary general meeting of HAC's shareholders (more than 200 of them) approved a capital increase in May 2026 to strengthen equity ahead of the DNCG hearing. Blue Crow, holding more than 95%, committed €18m and also provided guarantees and a blocked shareholder current-account contribution. On 10 June 2026 the DNCG imposed no restrictive measure on the club, the first time since June 2023.

name: Havre Athletic Club
notes: The earlier record's capacity (25,178, footballgroundmap) is replaced by the stadium page's 25,181 seats in football configuration; the club's Organisation & Infrastructures page gives 25,178. The club website is now hac.football (hac-foot.com redirects there). Financials come from the LFP/DNCG individual club accounts for 2024/25 (k€, consolidated SASP + association + SCI + subsidiaries). Player trading (+10,383 k€) cut the -20,219 k€ operating result before transfers to a -9,693 k€ pre-tax loss. The DNCG balance sheet shows negative equity of -22,534 k€, financial debts of 23,435 k€ and cash of 1,183 k€; net debt is not stated, so it is left null. Blue Crow's stake is the 96.21% it bought; Foot Normand gave more than 95% in May 2026, before the €18m capital increase closed, and the post-increase stake is not published. The purchase price was never disclosed. Headlines in July 2026 (Houston Business Journal, Paris-Normandie) report dueling lawsuits in Texas over the sale; their text could not be read. L'Équipe headlines say co-founder Jeff Luhnow left Blue Crow in June 2026; the club names Ben Guill as Blue Crow's chief executive and owner of HAC. HAC has no separate chief executive on its site: Jean-Michel Roussier is president, and Demba Ba joined as director of football in June 2026. No valuation, attendance average, kit supplier or social count was read on a citable page.

ownership_summary: Blue Crow Sports Group, a US multi-club investment group (chief executive Ben Guill; co-founded by Jeff Luhnow and Arvind Narayan), has been HAC's majority shareholder since July 2025. It bought the 96.21% held by Texan businessman Vincent Volpe, who had owned the club since 2015. In May 2026 Foot Normand put Blue Crow's stake at more than 95%, among more than 200 shareholders, and Blue Crow put €18m into a capital increase approved that month. UAE-based fund 885 Capital was reported in 2025 to co-own Blue Crow. In June 2026 Blue Crow sold its 84.21% of CD Leganés to 885 Capital and said it remained committed to HAC for the long term.
